newsitem.title: JAPAN: China officials now suspected illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: China officials now suspected illegal immigrants.

text.p: Japanese police said on Thursday they were searching for six missing members of a Chinese farm delegation who are suspected of joining a recent rush of Chinese illegal immigrants to Japan.

Police in Yamagata, northern Japan, said the six Chinese farm and livestock experts from the northeast province of Heilongjiang were last seen aboard a train headed for Tokyo at Yamagata city's main railway station on March 7.
The delegation arrived in Japan on February 28 and was expected to fly back to China on March 11, police said. The visas of its members expired on March 14.

Police said the delegation's host, the Yamagata Institute for Japan-China Friendship, received a statement from Heilongjiang provincial officials apologising for the fact that the Chinese apparently disappeared to seek jobs in Japan.
"It looks like the six never intended to come back to China," the statement from the Heilongjiang External Technology Commission said, according to police.
In the first two months of this year, a record 581 illegal Chinese immigrants were arrested by Japanese authorities, topping the 545 arrests for all of last year.
Many illegal immigrants have come in boats from Fujian and other densely populated coastal areas of China, lured by the prospect of high wages in Japan.
In a crackdown on groups suspected of bringing in the Chinese, Japanese police last month arrested seven suspected members of a Japan-based gang of illegal immigrant smugglers.
Earlier this week, the Justice Ministry unveiled plans to boost the maximum jail term for smuggling workers into the country from 18 months to 10 years.
Fines for human-smugglers also will rise to a maximum of 10 million yen ($81,300) from 150,000 yen ($1,219), the spokesman told reporters.
The proposed revisions to the Immigration Control Law will be submitted to parliament for enactment this month.
Under current law, penalties for smugglers are lighter than those for illegal entrants themselves.
